baits.label: The Abstract (6th Sense)
baits.profile: barrel-shaped body with flat ends; wide flat appendages; urchin-style
baits.note: urchin-style plastic with a Neko nail-weight slot; owner cross-refs: Hideout Coike, Berkley Omoeba
baits.rigging_rule: the hook needs to be larger/wider than the central ball of that kind of bait; if the hook doesn't extend beyond that central ball, you will lose fish or miss your hookset
field_notes: owner rig: 24mm green/blue Abstract, 3/0 treble hook, two 1/8 oz tungsten screw neko-style weights (1/4 oz total)
owner: medium-heavy rod required — lighter rods feel loaded like weeds; casting is challenging (poor aerodynamics)
owner: bite is sudden, hookup instant/hard
owner buoyancy: neutral — TPE urchin baits weigh a bit but won't sink unless weighted (maker copy says 'floating')
Jack's setup (2026-09-13): 24mm green pumpkin blue Abstract, 1/0 treble, 3/16 oz VMC neko weight — 12 lb (lake-record class) plus 7/6/5/3/3 in one Sunday session
Jack's line (2026-09-13): braid tied directly to the hook with no leader — against the finesse-leader convention, and it still produced the 12 lb

citations.quote: The Abstract takes the proven urchin-style profile and pushes it further with increased water displacement, responsive appendage action, and exceptional rigging versatility.
Available in 12mm, 18mm, 24mm, and 28mm sizes, the lineup scales from subtle finesse presentations for pressured fish to larger offerings designed to attract quality bites.
At the center of the design is a distinctive barrel-shaped body with flat ends that helps maintain a stable, natural posture throughout the presentation.
An integrated weight slot simplifies rigging with Neko nail weights, hooks, and other terminal tackle

runs a 24mm Abstract in green/blue with a 3/0 treble hook and two 1/8 oz tungsten screw neko-style weights (1/4 oz total)
you need a medium-heavy rod to run that, otherwise it feels like you have weeds on the line all the time
